coverage_states.covered: Provision present and consistent with standard form
coverage_states.covered_unfavorable: Present but materially one-sided against tenant
coverage_states.partial: Some expected elements present, others missing or weakened
coverage_states.ambiguous: Present but interpretation-dependent; practical effect unclear
coverage_states.missing: Issue area expected in this lease but provision is absent
coverage_states.broken_xref: Provision references a section, exhibit, or defined term not found in the document
coverage_states.potentially_unenforceable: Structural or legal defect that may limit enforceability
coverage_states.review_needed: Insufficient evidence to assert a state; surface for human judgment
coverage_states.not_applicable: Issue area does not apply to this lease based on exclusion clues or document type
coverage_states.applicability_unclear: Cannot determine whether this issue area should be present; needs human judgment

applicability_levels.required: Expected in every retail/commercial lease of this type
applicability_levels.conditional: Expected only when specific indicators are present in the document
applicability_levels.optional: May or may not be present; absence is not a concern without other signals

caution_signal_definitions.common_dispute_area: Frequently litigated provision type; outcome heavily fact-dependent
caution_signal_definitions.governing_law_sensitive: Practical effect varies significantly by jurisdiction
caution_signal_definitions.landlord_leverage_point: Landlord typically holds stronger enforcement position if disputed
caution_signal_definitions.tenant_leverage_point: Tenant holds strong position; landlord enforcement limited
caution_signal_definitions.potentially_unenforceable: Known structural defect or clause pattern with enforceability concerns
caution_signal_definitions.cascade_risk: Change to this provision may silently affect other provisions via cross-reference

issue_areas.name: Rent & Payment Terms
expected_elements: base rent amount or formula
payment due date (day of month)
late payment fee or penalty mechanism
grace period for late payment
accepted payment methods
additional rent definition (what constitutes additional rent)

coverage_state_rules.missing: No rent provision found in document
coverage_state_rules.partial: Base rent defined but late fee, due date, or additional rent definition absent
coverage_state_rules.broken_xref: References rent schedule or exhibit not present in document
coverage_state_rules.covered_unfavorable: Late fee grace period removed or shortened below 5 days

issue_areas.risk_if_missing: No enforceable rent obligation; landlord has no clear basis for payment demand or default notice
issue_areas.exposure_statement: Tenant's payment obligation and enforcement timeline undefined; creates ambiguity in default proceedings
negative_space_clues: Section marked 'Reserved' or 'Intentionally Omitted'
Reference to 'Exhibit A ג€” Rent Schedule' with no Exhibit A attached
Blank dollar amount placeholder not filled in
common_tenant_modifications: Grace period extensions (5 days ג†’ 10 days)
Reduced late fee percentage
Removal of additional rent catch-all definition

expected_elements_305.element_label: Base rent amount or formula is stated
expected_elements_305.review_notes: Fundamental lease term. Absence renders the lease potentially unenforceable.

expected_elements_305.element_label: Payment due date is specified
synonyms: payable on the first day of each
due on the first of each month
expected_elements_305.review_notes: Without a due date, landlord cannot establish late payment default.

expected_elements_305.element_label: Late payment fee or penalty mechanism is defined
expected_elements_305.review_notes: Enforceability of late fees varies by jurisdiction. Some states cap at a percentage.

expected_elements_305.element_label: Grace period for late payment is specified
synonyms: days after the date when due
expected_elements_305.review_notes: Without a grace period, tenant is in default immediately on the due date.

expected_elements_305.element_label: Accepted payment methods are specified
synonyms: by check, wire transfer, or ACH
to such account as Landlord may designate
expected_elements_305.review_notes: Low materiality. Most leases specify; absence is not a gap.

expected_elements_305.element_label: Additional rent is defined (what constitutes additional rent beyond base)
synonyms: all sums payable by Tenant other than Base Rent
the term Rent shall mean Base Rent and Additional Rent
CAM Charges, insurance, taxes shall constitute Additional Rent
expected_elements_305.review_notes: Defines what landlord can pursue as 'rent' in a default action. Broad definitions increase tenant exposure.

issue_areas.name: Rent Escalation
issue_areas.notes: Absence may be intentional (flat-rent leases).
expected_elements: annual increase mechanism (fixed percentage or CPI)
escalation cap or ceiling
effective date of first escalation
calculation methodology

coverage_state_rules.missing: No escalation provision found and no flat-rent exclusion language present
coverage_state_rules.partial: Escalation mechanism defined but cap or calculation method absent
coverage_state_rules.ambiguous: CPI reference present but index not specified
coverage_state_rules.covered_unfavorable: No cap on CPI increases
coverage_state_rules.not_applicable: Document explicitly states rent is fixed for the full term

issue_areas.risk_if_missing: Rent frozen at initial amount for entire term; landlord loses inflation protection

exposure_statement.tenant: No rent escalation cap; tenant bears uncapped exposure to inflation-driven rent increases over the lease term
exposure_statement.landlord: No rent escalation cap; landlord retains pricing flexibility but bears the dispute risk that comes with uncapped or formula-driven increases
exposure_statement.neutral: Rent escalation lacks a cap or fully defined calculation methodology; future rent increases may become disputed or difficult to price over the lease term

negative_space_clues: Escalation section header present but body blank or marked Reserved
Cross-reference to CPI index definition absent from Definitions article
common_tenant_modifications: CPI cap addition (e.g. maximum 3% per year)
Fixed-percentage substituted for uncapped CPI
First escalation deferred one year

expected_elements_305.element_label: Annual rent increase mechanism is defined (fixed percentage, CPI, or formula)
expected_elements_305.review_notes: Without a defined mechanism, escalation disputes are common. Fixed percentage is most predictable.

expected_elements_305.element_label: Effective date of first escalation is specified
synonyms: beginning on the second Lease Year
expected_elements_305.review_notes: Ambiguity on when escalation starts creates billing disputes.

expected_elements_305.element_label: Escalation cap or ceiling limits annual increases
synonyms: not to exceed percent per year
expected_elements_305.review_notes: Absence means uncapped exposure. CPI-based escalation without a cap is particularly risky in inflationary periods.

expected_elements_305.element_label: Calculation methodology for escalation is clear and verifiable
expected_elements_305.review_notes: Ambiguous methodology (compounded vs simple, which CPI index) creates billing disputes.

issue_areas.name: Lease Term & Renewal
expected_elements: initial term duration
commencement date or conditions
expiration date
renewal option count and duration
renewal notice period and deadline
rent at renewal (formula or fair market value mechanism)

coverage_state_rules.missing: No term provision found
coverage_state_rules.partial: Term defined but renewal options, notice periods, or renewal rent mechanism absent
coverage_state_rules.ambiguous: Renewal at 'fair market value' with no determination mechanism defined
coverage_state_rules.broken_xref: References commencement conditions defined in Work Letter or exhibit not present
coverage_state_rules.covered_unfavorable: Renewal notice period unusually short (under 90 days)

issue_areas.risk_if_missing: Lease duration undefined; tenancy may be at-will or interpreted as month-to-month

exposure_statement.tenant: Term and renewal rights unclear; tenant may lose right to remain in premises or face holdover penalties
exposure_statement.landlord: Renewal mechanism undefined; landlord faces uncertainty over future occupancy and has weakened leverage to reset rent or terms at expiration
exposure_statement.neutral: Lease term and renewal rights are incompletely defined; the absence of a renewal rent mechanism leaves both occupancy continuity and pricing unresolved at expiration

negative_space_clues: Renewal option section header with body struck or marked Reserved
Reference to 'Option to Renew' in Table of Contents but section absent from body
common_tenant_modifications: Extended notice period for renewal (90 days ג†’ 12 months)
Added renewal options (1 ג†’ 2 or 3)
Capped renewal rent at fixed percentage over expiring rent

expected_elements_305.element_label: Initial term duration is stated
expected_elements_305.review_notes: Fundamental lease term.

expected_elements_305.element_label: Commencement date or conditions for commencement are defined
expected_elements_305.review_notes: Conditional commencement (tied to construction completion) creates date uncertainty.

expected_elements_305.element_label: Expiration date or method to determine it is stated
expected_elements_305.review_notes: Must be determinable even if not a fixed date.

expected_elements_305.element_label: Renewal option count and duration are specified
expected_elements_305.review_notes: Absence means tenant has no right to stay beyond initial term.

expected_elements_305.element_label: Renewal notice period and deadline are specified
synonyms: months prior to the Expiration Date
exercise such renewal option by delivering
expected_elements_305.review_notes: Missed deadline typically means waiver of renewal right. Short deadlines without landlord reminder obligation are tenant-unfavorable.

expected_elements_305.element_label: Rent at renewal is defined (formula, fair market value, or fixed)
synonyms: Base Rent during the Renewal Term shall be
expected_elements_305.review_notes: Without a defined renewal rent, the renewal option may be unenforceable or subject to landlord's unilateral pricing.

issue_areas.name: Security Deposit
issue_areas.notes: Bare 'security' removed from activation_clues v1.1.1 ג€” too broad.
expected_elements: deposit amount
return deadline after lease expiration
permitted deduction conditions
interest obligation (if any)
letter of credit alternative conditions

coverage_state_rules.missing: Deposit referenced in lease header or recitals but no deposit provision found
coverage_state_rules.partial: Amount defined but return timeline or deduction conditions absent
coverage_state_rules.covered_unfavorable: Return deadline unusually long (over 60 days)
coverage_state_rules.not_applicable: No deposit references found anywhere in document

issue_areas.risk_if_missing: If deposit was negotiated, landlord has no documented security mechanism
issue_areas.exposure_statement: Deposit obligation referenced but terms undefined; return and deduction rights unprotected
negative_space_clues: Deposit amount shown as blank or $0.00 in lease summary
Letter of credit alternative referenced but terms not defined
common_tenant_modifications: Reduced deposit amount
Burn-down schedule (deposit reduces over time)
Shortened return deadline

expected_elements_305.element_label: Deposit amount is stated
synonyms: security deposit in the amount of
expected_elements_305.review_notes: Fundamental term.

expected_elements_305.element_label: Return deadline after lease expiration is specified
expected_elements_305.review_notes: Many states have statutory return deadlines (14-60 days). Lease term should match or improve on statutory minimum.

expected_elements_305.element_label: Permitted deduction conditions are defined
expected_elements_305.review_notes: Broad deduction language without itemization requirement is tenant-unfavorable.

expected_elements_305.element_label: Interest obligation on deposit is addressed
synonyms: Landlord shall not be required to pay interest
expected_elements_305.review_notes: Some jurisdictions require interest on deposits by statute.

expected_elements_305.element_label: Letter of credit or alternative security form is addressed
synonyms: letter of credit in lieu of
expected_elements_305.review_notes: Relevant for larger deposits where cash tie-up is material. Common in institutional leases.

issue_areas.name: Permitted Use
issue_areas.notes: Cascade risk: force majeure definition changes can alter continuous operation obligations.
expected_elements: specific permitted use description
continuous operation obligation
prohibited use restrictions
co-tenancy or anchor dependency language

coverage_state_rules.missing: No permitted use provision
coverage_state_rules.partial: Use defined but continuous operation, prohibited use restrictions, or co-tenancy language absent
coverage_state_rules.ambiguous: Use defined broadly without specific business description
coverage_state_rules.broken_xref: Permitted use cross-references definition not present in document
coverage_state_rules.covered_unfavorable: Continuous operation obligation present with no force majeure carve-out

issue_areas.risk_if_missing: No restriction on how tenant uses space; may conflict with other tenant exclusives in the center
issue_areas.exposure_statement: Use restrictions absent or undefined; tenant may face exclusive use violations or continuous operation penalties
negative_space_clues: Exclusive use clause header present but body blank
Reference to 'Exhibit B ג€” Exclusive Use Area' with no exhibit attached
common_tenant_modifications: Broadened permitted use description
Weakened continuous operation obligation (shall ג†’ may)
Added co-tenancy condition tied to anchor tenant

expected_elements_305.element_label: Specific permitted use description is stated
synonyms: Tenant shall use the Premises solely for
use and occupy the Premises for
expected_elements_305.review_notes: Overly narrow use clauses restrict tenant flexibility. Overly broad clauses weaken landlord's tenant mix control.

expected_elements_305.element_label: Continuous operation obligation is addressed
expected_elements_305.review_notes: Continuous operation without a go-dark right prevents tenant from closing during renovations or downturns.

expected_elements_305.element_label: Prohibited uses are defined
synonyms: Tenant shall not use the Premises for any purpose that is unlawful
no use that disturbs other tenants
expected_elements_305.review_notes: Standard boilerplate. Overly broad prohibited use lists can trap tenants.

expected_elements_305.element_label: Co-tenancy or anchor tenant dependency is addressed
expected_elements_305.review_notes: Primarily relevant for retail in shopping centers. Cross-LP with LP-31 Co-Tenancy.

issue_areas.name: Maintenance & Repairs
expected_elements: tenant maintenance obligations (interior, non-structural)
landlord maintenance obligations (structural, roof, exterior)
HVAC responsibility allocation
repair response time obligations
damage and destruction repair process

coverage_state_rules.missing: No maintenance allocation provision
coverage_state_rules.partial: General allocation present but HVAC, structural, or response times absent
coverage_state_rules.covered_unfavorable: Tenant bears HVAC replacement cost with no age or condition cap
coverage_state_rules.ambiguous: HVAC responsibility stated as 'shared' without clear allocation formula

issue_areas.risk_if_missing: Maintenance obligations default to tenant under many jurisdictions
issue_areas.exposure_statement: Maintenance allocation undefined; tenant may bear unexpected capital repair costs including structural and HVAC replacement
negative_space_clues: HVAC section header present but body struck or blank
Landlord repair obligation section marked Reserved
common_tenant_modifications: Landlord bears HVAC replacement cost above threshold amount
Structural repair obligation shifted to landlord

expected_elements_305.element_label: Tenant maintenance obligations are defined (interior, non-structural)
synonyms: at Tenant's sole cost and expense, maintain
Tenant responsible for interior walls, floors, fixtures
expected_elements_305.review_notes: Without clear allocation, both parties claim the other is responsible.

expected_elements_305.element_label: Landlord maintenance obligations are defined (structural, roof, exterior)
synonyms: Landlord shall maintain the structural elements
expected_elements_305.review_notes: In NNN leases, structural maintenance may be passed through as CAM. Tenant should verify.

expected_elements_305.element_label: HVAC responsibility allocation is defined
synonyms: Landlord responsible for major HVAC repairs
expected_elements_305.review_notes: HVAC is the most disputed maintenance item. Split between routine (tenant) and capital replacement (landlord) is market.

expected_elements_305.element_label: Repair response time obligations are stated
expected_elements_305.review_notes: Without a defined timeline, tenant has no leverage for delayed repairs.

expected_elements_305.element_label: Damage and destruction repair process is defined
synonyms: in the event of damage or destruction
expected_elements_305.review_notes: Often covered in LP-24 Damage & Destruction. Cross-LP coverage acceptable.

issue_areas.name: Common Area Maintenance (CAM)
issue_areas.notes: Not applicable in gross or full-service leases.
expected_elements: tenant's proportionate share calculation method
included expense categories
excluded expense categories
annual CAM increase cap
tenant audit rights
reconciliation timeline

coverage_state_rules.missing: CAM references present in lease but no CAM provision found
coverage_state_rules.partial: Share calculation present but exclusions, cap, or audit rights absent
coverage_state_rules.covered_unfavorable: No annual CAM cap; audit rights absent or time-limited to 30 days
coverage_state_rules.ambiguous: Proportionate share defined by landlord's reasonable determination with no formula
coverage_state_rules.not_applicable: Gross or full-service lease structure confirmed

issue_areas.risk_if_missing: Tenant may owe undefined share of all building operating expenses with no audit protection
issue_areas.exposure_statement: CAM exposure uncapped and unauditable; tenant cannot verify or challenge operating expense pass-throughs
negative_space_clues: CAM cap provision header present but percentage blank
Audit rights section marked Reserved or Intentionally Omitted
Excluded expenses list cross-references exhibit not attached
common_tenant_modifications: 5% annual CAM increase cap added
Capital expenditure exclusion added
Management fee cap (typically 15% of operating expenses)

expected_elements_305.element_label: Tenant's proportionate share calculation method is defined
synonyms: numerator of which is the rentable area
expected_elements_305.review_notes: Denominator definition matters: total center vs occupied space. Occupied-only denominator shifts vacant space costs to existing tenants.

expected_elements_305.element_label: Included expense categories are enumerated
expected_elements_305.review_notes: 'Including without limitation' language makes the list illustrative, not exhaustive. Tenant-unfavorable.

expected_elements_305.element_label: Excluded expense categories are defined
expected_elements_305.review_notes: Without exclusions, landlord can pass through capital improvements, legal fees, and overhead. Major tenant risk.

expected_elements_305.element_label: Annual CAM increase cap is defined
synonyms: CAM Charges shall not increase by more than
expected_elements_305.review_notes: Absence means uncapped CAM exposure. Controllable vs non-controllable split is market standard.

expected_elements_305.element_label: Tenant audit rights for CAM charges are defined
synonyms: Tenant shall have the right to audit
Tenant shall not have the right to audit
expected_elements_305.review_notes: Explicit denial of audit rights is covered_unfavorable. Absence without explicit denial is a gap.

expected_elements_305.element_label: Annual reconciliation timeline is specified
synonyms: within ninety days after the end of each calendar year
expected_elements_305.review_notes: Without a reconciliation deadline, landlord can delay true-ups indefinitely.

issue_areas.name: Insurance Requirements
expected_elements: tenant commercial general liability minimum ($1M per occurrence, $2M aggregate standard)
property insurance obligation
business interruption coverage
landlord as additional insured
certificate of insurance delivery obligation
waiver of subrogation

coverage_state_rules.missing: No insurance provision
coverage_state_rules.partial: Liability minimum present but additional insured, property coverage, or waiver of subrogation absent
coverage_state_rules.covered_unfavorable: Coverage minimums unusually high; waiver of subrogation absent
coverage_state_rules.potentially_unenforceable: Named insured requirement conflicts with standard policy structure

issue_areas.risk_if_missing: Tenant may operate uninsured; landlord has no recourse against tenant insurer for losses

exposure_statement.tenant: Insurance obligations incompletely defined; tenant may face uncovered losses and disputed coverage scope without a clear subrogation waiver
exposure_statement.landlord: Insurance obligations incompletely defined; landlord lacks reliable recourse against tenant insurers for premises-related losses and has no subrogation waiver to limit cross-claims
exposure_statement.neutral: Insurance requirements are incomplete; the missing waiver of subrogation leaves either party exposed to recovery actions by the other's insurer following a covered loss

negative_space_clues: Waiver of subrogation section present but obligation direction reversed or blank
Certificate delivery obligation cross-references deleted notice section
common_tenant_modifications: Reduced minimum coverage amounts
Removal of business interruption requirement
Mutual waiver of subrogation (one-way ג†’ two-way)

expected_elements_305.element_label: Commercial general liability minimum coverage is specified
synonyms: commercial general liability insurance with limits of not less than
expected_elements_305.review_notes: Market standard: $1M/$2M. Higher limits for larger spaces or higher-risk uses.

expected_elements_305.element_label: Property insurance obligation is defined
synonyms: property insurance covering Tenant's personal property
expected_elements_305.review_notes: Tenant's property insurance protects tenant's investment. Landlord's property insurance covers the building.

expected_elements_305.element_label: Business interruption insurance coverage is addressed
expected_elements_305.review_notes: Protects tenant's ability to pay rent during interruption. Connects to LP-14 Force Majeure and LP-24 Damage.

expected_elements_305.element_label: Landlord is named as additional insured on tenant's policies
synonyms: Landlord, Landlord's managing agent, and Landlord's lender
expected_elements_305.review_notes: Standard requirement. Lender as additional insured is also common.

expected_elements_305.element_label: Certificate of insurance delivery obligation is defined
synonyms: days prior to expiration of each policy
expected_elements_305.review_notes: Procedural requirement.

expected_elements_305.element_label: Mutual waiver of subrogation is included
synonyms: waives any right of recovery against the other party
to the extent covered by insurance
expected_elements_305.review_notes: Without mutual waiver, insurer can pursue the other party after paying a claim. One-way waiver is unfavorable to the waiving party.

issue_areas.name: Subletting & Assignment
expected_elements: landlord consent requirement
grounds for withholding consent (reasonableness standard)
affiliate exception (no consent required for related entities)
profit sharing on sublet above base rent
recapture right (landlord can terminate and lease directly)
assignment in connection with sale of business

coverage_state_rules.missing: No assignment provision
coverage_state_rules.partial: Consent requirement present but affiliate exception, recapture, or profit sharing absent
coverage_state_rules.covered_unfavorable: Landlord consent in sole and absolute discretion; no affiliate exception
coverage_state_rules.potentially_unenforceable: Landlord consent in 'sole and absolute discretion' WITHOUT reasonableness standard ג€” unenforceable in jurisdictions implying good faith and reasonableness in commercial leases (escalation governed by jurisdiction_rules; see governing_law_sensitive caution signal)
coverage_state_rules.broken_xref: Affiliate defined by cross-reference to definition section not present in document

issue_areas.risk_if_missing: Assignment rights undefined; tenant unable to sell business or transfer lease in routine transactions
issue_areas.exposure_statement: Assignment rights absent or over-restricted; tenant cannot execute routine business transactions including sale of business
negative_space_clues: Affiliate exception section marked Reserved
Sale-of-business exception cross-references deleted exhibit
Consent provision uses 'sole and absolute discretion' or 'absolute discretion' without 'reasonably' or 'commercially reasonable' qualifier
common_tenant_modifications: Reasonableness standard added ('not unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed')
Affiliate exception broadened (parent, subsidiary, successor entities)
Sale-of-business exception expanded to include asset sales

expected_elements_305.element_label: Assignment requires landlord consent
synonyms: Tenant shall not assign this Lease without Landlord's prior written consent
No assignment shall be made without Landlord consent
Assignment subject to Landlord's prior approval
Tenant may not transfer its interest in this Lease without Landlord approval
expected_elements_305.review_notes: Pattern A: explicit text required. A lease silent on assignment consent may materially weaken landlord control over tenant identity and creditworthiness; no alternate coverage path is acceptable.

expected_elements_305.element_label: Subletting requires landlord consent
synonyms: Tenant shall not sublet all or any portion of the Premises without Landlord's prior written consent
No sublease shall be entered into without Landlord consent
Subletting subject to Landlord's prior approval
Tenant may not sublease the Premises without Landlord approval
expected_elements_305.review_notes: Pattern A: explicit text required. Assignment and subletting must be separate elements because one can be restricted while the other is omitted or treated differently.

expected_elements_305.element_label: Consent standard is supplied by lease text or applicable default law
synonyms: Landlord may withhold consent in its sole and absolute discretion
Landlord's consent shall not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed
Landlord may grant or deny consent in its reasonable discretion
Consent may be withheld for any reason or no reason
expected_elements_305.review_notes: Pattern B: lease text strongly preferred but jurisdiction may supply a default. Renamed from consent_standard_defined (v0.1) because default law does not 'define' the lease term — it supplies a fallback standard. The renamed element captures both paths cleanly. Polarity is contextual: sole-discretion language is landlord-favorable; reasonable-not-to-be-withheld is tenant-favorable. If absent and jurisdiction supplies a default, exposure layer should note 'consent standard supplied by [jurisdiction default rule]; explicit drafting recommended.' Attorney review needed before populating state list.

expected_elements_305.element_label: Affiliate or related-party transfer exception is defined or excluded
synonyms: transfer to a parent, subsidiary, or commonly controlled entity
merger, consolidation, or sale of substantially all assets
expected_elements_305.review_notes: Pattern B: implicit coverage acceptable (broad consent-with-exceptions language can satisfy). Absence means tenant cannot freely transfer to affiliates. From landlord perspective, broad presence of affiliate exceptions may be unfavorable; this element's absence vs presence is perspective-sensitive at the exposure layer, but absence_adverse_to is tenant because absence removes a tenant-side flexibility.

expected_elements_305.element_label: Change of control is addressed
synonyms: change in control shall be deemed an assignment
direct or indirect transfer of control
expected_elements_305.review_notes: No alternate coverage paths open; explicit_drafting_preferred is moot. Especially relevant for entity tenants. If absent, tenant may transfer practical control without triggering the assignment clause.

expected_elements_305.element_label: Original tenant remains liable after assignment or sublease
synonyms: No assignment or subletting shall release Tenant
Tenant shall not be relieved of its obligations
Tenant remains responsible for all covenants and obligations
expected_elements_305.review_notes: Pattern B (v0.2 correction): originally must_be_explicit=true with cross_LP_coverage=[LP-11] — internally contradictory. Resolved by making must_be_explicit=false plus explicit_drafting_preferred=true. The 'explicit preferred' intent is now expressed by the soft signal plus high absence_severity. Cross-LP coverage to LP-11 (continuing liability via breach-of-covenant theory) is allowed if Step 305 cites the actual LP-11 provision; chanting 'cross-LP' is not coverage.

expected_elements_305.element_label: Assignee or subtenant must assume lease obligations
synonyms: assignee shall assume all obligations under this Lease
subtenant shall comply with all terms of this Lease
assignment agreement must include assumption of obligations
such Affiliate assumes all obligations of Tenant under this Lease
assignee or subtenant assumes all obligations
assumes Tenant's obligations under this Lease
subject to all terms and conditions of the Lease, including assumption
expected_elements_305.review_notes: Pattern A: explicit text required. Separate from original-tenant-continuing-liability. Both can be true, one can be missing, or both can be absent absence_severity lowered to medium (2026-05-11 305d): assumption of obligations is often supplied by contract law; absence is a drafting preference issue rather than a high-severity gap. In leases where assumption language appears only in the Affiliate-transfer exception (not the general consent case), the element is partially satisfied; evaluators should return explicitly_present for the subset covered or implicitly_present if the general principle is inferable, rather than missing or unclear.

expected_elements_305.element_label: Landlord recapture or termination right upon proposed transfer
synonyms: Landlord may terminate this Lease as to the proposed transfer space
expected_elements_305.review_notes: No alternate coverage paths. Optional landlord-favorable control right. Absence is not necessarily a defect; presence may be unfavorable from tenant perspective at the exposure layer.

expected_elements_305.element_label: Transfer profits or excess rent are allocated

expected_elements_305.review_notes: No alternate coverage paths. Absence is landlord-unfavorable but not core coverage failure. If present, the percentage and calculation method matter for the exposure layer.

expected_elements_305.element_label: Unauthorized transfers are void, default-triggering, or otherwise remedied

Violation of this section is a default

Resolved by making must_be_explicit=false plus explicit_drafting_preferred=true. Can be covered directly in LP-09 explicitly, implicitly via broad-consequences language, or by cross-LP to LP-11 if breach of any lease covenant is an event of default. Step 305 must cite the actual default provision if relying on cross-LP coverage.

subtenant shall use the Premises only for the Permitted Use
assignment subject to all restrictions in this Lease
expected_elements_305.review_notes: Pattern B: explicit preferred but alternates acceptable. Can be implicit if assignee/subtenant assumption language is broad enough. If relying on LP-05, the evaluator must cite both the transfer provision and the permitted-use clause.

issue_areas.name: Default & Remedies
expected_elements: monetary default definition and cure period (typically 5 days)
non-monetary default definition and cure period (typically 30 days)
notice requirement before default declaration
landlord termination right
landlord re-entry right
tenant's right to cure third-party defaults
rent acceleration on default

coverage_state_rules.missing: No default provision
coverage_state_rules.partial: Monetary default present but non-monetary default, notice requirement, or cure period absent
coverage_state_rules.covered_unfavorable: Cure period unusually short (under 30 days for non-monetary); OR landlord remedies aggressive but conditioned on prior notice and cure opportunity
coverage_state_rules.broken_xref: Remedies cross-reference deleted exhibit or section
coverage_state_rules.potentially_unenforceable: Self-help re-entry language permitting landlord to re-enter and remove tenant or property without judicial process AND without explicit reservation of tenant's right to legal process; covered_unfavorable governs when re-entry language is aggressive but conditioned on notice and cure

issue_areas.notes: Rule precedence v1.1.4: covered_unfavorable governs aggressive remedies that are still gated by notice/cure procedures. potentially_unenforceable is reserved for self-help language that bypasses judicial process entirely. When both could arguably apply, covered_unfavorable is the safer default; potentially_unenforceable should require explicit absence of legal-process reservation (e.g. clause states landlord 'may re-enter without legal process' or equivalent).
issue_areas.risk_if_missing: Landlord remedies limited to common law; no contractual right to accelerate rent or re-enter
issue_areas.exposure_statement: Default and remedy framework absent or incomplete; landlord enforcement position significantly weakened
negative_space_clues: Remedy section header present but acceleration clause absent
Notice requirement section marked Reserved
common_tenant_modifications: Extended cure periods (5 days ג†’ 10 days monetary; 30 days ג†’ 45 days non-monetary)
Notice required before every default declaration
Added third-party cure right (mortgagee or guarantor may cure)

expected_elements_305.element_label: Monetary default is defined (what triggers default for non-payment)
synonyms: failure to pay rent when due
Tenant shall be in default if Tenant fails to pay any Rent or other sum
an Event of Default shall mean failure to pay any Rent
if Tenant fails to make any payment when due
expected_elements_305.review_notes: Pattern A: explicit text required. Without a defined monetary default trigger, landlord has no contractual basis to act on missed rent. Default law doesn't supply a remedy structure absent the lease defining what counts as default.

expected_elements_305.element_label: Non-monetary default is defined (breach of covenants other than payment)
synonyms: failure to perform any covenant or obligation other than the payment of Rent
default in the performance of any other term, covenant, or condition
any other breach of this Lease
Tenant fails to comply with any other provision
expected_elements_305.review_notes: Pattern A: explicit text required. Separate from monetary because cure periods and remedies typically differ. Real leases sometimes omit a general non-monetary default category and only enumerate specific covenants, which is structurally incomplete.

expected_elements_305.element_label: Tenant bankruptcy or insolvency is a default event
synonyms: Tenant files a petition in bankruptcy
assignment for the benefit of creditors
Tenant's bankruptcy or insolvency shall constitute an Event of Default
expected_elements_305.review_notes: Optional element; no alternate coverage paths. Common but not universal. Bankruptcy code may limit landlord's practical ability to enforce ipso facto clauses, but having the clause is still landlord-favorable for cure period defaulting and pre-petition leverage.

expected_elements_305.element_label: Cure period for monetary default is specified
synonyms: Tenant shall have five (5) days after written notice to cure
if Tenant fails to pay within three (3) days after notice
expected_elements_305.review_notes: Pattern A: explicit text required. Beitel anchor element 1 of 3. The presence of a monetary cure period is tenant-favorable; absence means landlord can act on default immediately. Day count is quality-of-presence not severity-of-absence: a 3-day period is materially weaker tenant protection than a 10-day period, but both are 'present.' Quality nuance captured here in notes rather than as a new schema field.

expected_elements_305.element_label: Cure period for non-monetary default is specified
synonyms: thirty (30) days after written notice to cure
Tenant shall have thirty (30) days to cure any non-monetary default
such longer period as may be reasonably necessary to cure
expected_elements_305.review_notes: Pattern A: explicit text required. Typically longer than monetary cure (often 30 days). 'Such longer period as may be reasonably necessary' language is tenant-favorable extension for non-curable-in-30-days breaches. Absence of an extension clause without compensating language is weaker tenant protection.

expected_elements_305.element_label: Landlord must give notice of default to trigger cure period
synonyms: Landlord shall give Tenant written notice specifying the default
notice of default delivered in accordance with Section [Notices]
expected_elements_305.review_notes: Pattern A: explicit text required. Critical procedural protection. Without explicit notice requirement, cure period may begin running from the default event itself (or not exist), giving tenant no actual opportunity to cure. The notice-trigger requirement is what makes cure periods practically meaningful.

expected_elements_305.element_label: Landlord has right to terminate the lease upon uncured default
synonyms: Landlord shall have the right to terminate Tenant's right of possession
Landlord may declare this Lease terminated
right to terminate by written notice to Tenant
Landlord may at its option terminate this Lease
expected_elements_305.review_notes: Pattern A: explicit text required. Termination of the lease (extinguishing future obligations) is distinct from re-entry (taking back possession). Some jurisdictions and some leases treat these as one remedy; others as two. Pilot treats them as separate elements because the legal effects differ on accrued rent.

expected_elements_305.element_label: Landlord has right to re-enter and repossess the premises
synonyms: Landlord may re-enter and take possession
Landlord may enter upon the Premises and expel Tenant
with or without process of law
Landlord may take possession of the Premises
expected_elements_305.review_notes: Pattern A: explicit text required. The Beitel summary's claim that this was absent was demonstrably wrong — Article 15 contained explicit re-entry language. Per-element schema with mandatory citation prevents this kind of confident-wrong assertion: the LP-11.landlord_right_to_reenter_premises element must be cited or marked missing, and the citation requirement is what catches the error.

expected_elements_305.element_label: Landlord may accelerate remaining rent obligations upon default
synonyms: all Rent for the remainder of the Term shall become immediately due and payable
the present value of the remaining Rent shall be due and payable
accelerated Rent equal to the difference between Rent and fair market rental value
Tenant shall pay to Landlord the entire amount of Rent for the unexpired portion of the Term
expected_elements_305.review_notes: Pattern A: explicit text required. Beitel anchor element 2 of 3. Rent acceleration is not a default remedy in any US jurisdiction — it must be explicitly granted by lease language. The Beitel summary inverted this element by asserting absence; per-element schema with mandatory citation makes the inversion impossible: an evaluator must produce a verdict tied to specific lease text. Acceleration formulas (face value vs present-value-discounted) are quality-of-presence captured in notes, not a separate element.

expected_elements_305.element_label: Damages framework on termination is specified (calculation method, mitigation duty)
synonyms: Tenant shall be liable for all damages Landlord may suffer
Landlord's damages shall include the difference between the Rent reserved and the rent received
Landlord shall use commercially reasonable efforts to relet
Tenant's liability shall be reduced by amounts actually received from reletting
expected_elements_305.review_notes: Pattern B: implicit and default-law coverage acceptable. Mitigation duty varies by jurisdiction. Most US states impose a duty to mitigate by default in commercial leases; some do not. Jurisdiction list is attorney-blocked. Damages calculation method is conventionally implied (difference between reserved rent and mitigated re-letting income) but lease language clarifying this is preferred.

expected_elements_305.element_label: Landlord's reletting rights and obligations are specified
synonyms: Landlord may relet the Premises for the account of Tenant
Landlord shall have the right but not the obligation to relet
any reletting shall not constitute a waiver of Tenant's liability
Tenant shall be credited with any rentals actually received
expected_elements_305.review_notes: Pattern B: implicit and default-law coverage acceptable. Polarity is contextual. Mitigation-duty language is tenant-favorable; right-but-not-obligation language is landlord-favorable. Both can be present (mitigation duty AND right to relet on tenant's account) which is the typical balanced position. Default law often supplies mitigation duty by background rule.

expected_elements_305.element_label: Landlord has self-help right to cure tenant's default and bill tenant
synonyms: Landlord may but shall not be obligated to cure any default
amounts expended by Landlord shall be Additional Rent
Landlord may perform Tenant's obligations and Tenant shall reimburse
expected_elements_305.review_notes: Pattern A: explicit text required. Useful procedural remedy for non-monetary defaults where landlord needs the cure done. Common but not universal. Absence is not a serious LP coverage failure.

expected_elements_305.element_label: Common law and equitable remedies are preserved as additional remedies
synonyms: all remedies available at law or in equity
in addition to all remedies available at law or in equity
any other remedy now or hereafter available at law or in equity
Landlord shall have all remedies provided by law
expected_elements_305.review_notes: Pattern B: implicit coverage acceptable via the 'at law or in equity' legal idiom. Beitel anchor element 3 of 3 and the canonical implicit-coverage test case from the architecture spec. An evaluator must recognize 'at law or in equity' phrasing as implicit coverage. In most US jurisdictions, common-law remedies are preserved by default unless explicitly waived, so default_law_covers is jurisdiction-dependent and implicit_coverage_acceptable is true. The Beitel summary's inversion of this element ('limited to common law') was the most egregious inversion in the failure case — the actual lease used the standard preservation idiom.

expected_elements_305.element_label: Remedies are cumulative and not exclusive (landlord may pursue multiple)
synonyms: no remedy is intended to be exclusive
Landlord may pursue any one or more remedies
remedies are cumulative and may be exercised concurrently or successively
the exercise of any remedy shall not preclude the exercise of any other
expected_elements_305.review_notes: Pattern B: implicit coverage acceptable if multiple remedies are listed without 'exclusive' language. If absent, election-of-remedies doctrine may force landlord to pick one remedy and waive others. Most leases include this language explicitly. Default law in many jurisdictions treats remedies as cumulative unless lease makes one exclusive.

expected_elements_305.element_label: Abandonment or vacating as event of default
synonyms: vacating the Premises without commercially reasonable security
if Tenant ceases to occupy the Premises
expected_elements_305.review_notes: Explicitly named in AIR CRE Section 13.1. Absence means landlord has no specific contractual trigger for abandonment scenarios. Lower severity than monetary/non-monetary default definitions because abandonment can often be captured under the general non-monetary default category.

expected_elements_305.element_label: Extension of non-monetary cure period when cure is being diligently pursued
synonyms: such longer period as may be reasonably necessary provided Tenant has commenced cure
if cure cannot be completed within thirty days, Tenant shall have additional time
expected_elements_305.review_notes: AIR CRE Section 13.1(e) explicitly. Confirmed by California Lawyers Association and Baker Burton Lundy practitioner analyses. Without this, tenant can be defaulted for good-faith cure that takes longer than 30 days. Separate from cure_period_non_monetary because they receive different verdicts: cure period present + extension absent is a materially different state than both present.

expected_elements_305.element_label: Third-party (mortgagee or guarantor) cure right on tenant default
synonyms: mortgagee may cure on behalf of Tenant
Tenant's lender shall have the right to cure
Landlord shall give simultaneous notice to Tenant's mortgagee
expected_elements_305.review_notes: Common in institutional leases with SNDA. Cross-LP coverage to LP-22 is legitimate when the SNDA itself grants mortgagee cure rights. Lower severity because it is not present in all leases and its absence does not fundamentally weaken the default framework.

expected_elements_305.review_notes: Pattern A: explicit text required. If subordination requires tenant execution of documents (next element), self-executing language is typically absent or paired with the execution obligation. Both can coexist (self-executing AND tenant agrees to execute confirmation) which is the strongest landlord position.

expected_elements_305.review_notes: Pattern A: explicit text required. Practical mechanism for lender requirements. Often paired with a time limit (10-15 days) and a default consequence (treating non-execution as a breach). The execution deadline and default consequence are not split into separate elements at the pilot stage but may need to be if LP-11 reveals that default consequences should always be separate elements.

expected_elements_305.element_label: Lender will not disturb tenant's possession if landlord defaults under mortgage
synonyms: Lender agrees that Tenant's possession of the Premises shall not be disturbed
non-disturbance of Tenant's quiet enjoyment under this Lease
Tenant's right to occupy shall not be terminated upon foreclosure
this Lease shall continue in full force and effect notwithstanding foreclosure
expected_elements_305.review_notes: Pattern A: explicit text required. This is the §21.9 anchor case. Non-disturbance is tenant-favorable and structurally distinct from subordination. A lease may contain subordination without non-disturbance — the most common LP-22 coverage gap. Cross-LP coverage from LP-26 (Quiet Enjoyment) is explicitly NOT allowed: quiet enjoyment governs landlord conduct toward tenant during normal lease operation; non-disturbance governs lender or successor conduct toward tenant after foreclosure. The two are topically related but not coverage-substitutable. An evaluator that cites LP-26 to satisfy this element should be flagged as making an unsupported cross-LP claim.

expected_elements_305.element_label: Non-disturbance source is a binding agreement, not merely a future obligation

expected_elements_305.review_notes: Pattern A: explicit text required. A clause that says 'Landlord shall use commercially reasonable efforts to obtain a non-disturbance agreement' is materially weaker than 'Landlord has obtained' or 'Landlord shall obtain.' The pilot draft treats binding-source vs effort-based as a coverage distinction. Step 305 evaluators should cite the specific language that establishes the binding nature.

expected_elements_305.element_label: Landlord obligated to obtain non-disturbance from future lenders, not only existing

Tenant's subordination to future mortgages is conditioned upon delivery of an SNDA
subordinate to any mortgage now or hereafter placed, provided that the holder agrees not to disturb Tenant's possession
subordination to future mortgages conditioned on non-disturbance by holder
hereafter placed upon the premises, provided that holder agrees not to disturb
expected_elements_305.review_notes: Pattern A: explicit text required. Separates the future-mortgage protection from the existing-mortgage protection. A common gap: lease has SNDA from current lender but no commitment to obtain one from future lenders. Refinancing event then leaves tenant unprotected Also satisfied by a conditional-subordination clause: 'subordinate to any mortgage now or hereafter placed, provided that the holder agrees not to disturb Tenant's possession.' This pattern is explicit coverage of future lenders even without a separate Landlord-obtains-SNDA obligation. Evaluators must recognize the 'hereafter placed... provided that holder agrees' construct as satisfying this element via explicitly_present.

expected_elements_305.review_notes: Pattern A: explicit text required. Attornment is the lender/successor-favorable counterpart to non-disturbance. Without it, the successor has weak ability to enforce the lease as a continuing obligation. Conventionally bundled with subordination and non-disturbance but structurally distinct.

expected_elements_305.element_label: Attornment is automatic or self-executing without requiring tenant signature

expected_elements_305.review_notes: Pattern B: implicit coverage acceptable. If attornment is present but mechanism is not specified, the successor can typically still rely on Tenant's recognition as a matter of contract construction. Procedural detail.

expected_elements_305.review_notes: Pattern B (v0.2.1 correction): implicit_coverage_acceptable flipped from true to false because the legitimate alternate path is cross-LP-via-LP-11, not implicit-within-LP-22. The element bundles two sub-concepts (execution timing and consequence of non-execution), neither of which has a meaningful implicit-within-LP-22 path: an implicit deadline or implicit named consequence is structurally weak. If the execution-deadline clause is silent on consequences, default consequences may flow through LP-11 (breach of any covenant). The cross-LP reference is legitimate only if the LP-11 default provision actually captures execution failures, which the evaluator must cite. Same semantic confusion pattern as the LP-27.lender_notice_and_cure_right correction in v0.2.

The 'total loss' threshold determines which party can exit.

issue_areas.name: Quiet Enjoyment
issue_areas.notes: Required in every commercial lease. A fundamental landlord covenant ג€” its absence may be supplied by state law in many jurisdictions, but an express covenant is preferred to avoid jurisdictional ambiguity. The covenant should survive against lenders and successors for SNDA compatibility.
expected_elements: express quiet enjoyment covenant by landlord
covenant conditioned on tenant's performance of lease obligations (not absolute)
survival and binding effect on landlord's successors, assigns, and lenders
covenant not subject to any undisclosed superior lien or encumbrance

coverage_state_rules.ambiguous: Quiet enjoyment referenced without definition of scope or conditions
coverage_state_rules.covered_unfavorable: Covenant is conditioned on landlord's receipt of rent from tenant rather than tenant's compliance with all lease obligations; OR covenant explicitly does not bind lenders or successors in interest
coverage_state_rules.potentially_unenforceable: Quiet enjoyment covenant purports to be absolute (not conditioned on tenant's performance) ג€” may conflict with landlord's right to re-enter on tenant default

exposure_statement.tenant: Quiet enjoyment covenant absent or undefined; tenant's right to undisturbed possession depends on state law, which varies and may not protect against lender interference
exposure_statement.landlord: Quiet enjoyment covenant undefined; landlord faces uncertainty over scope of obligation and whether covenant binds successors, creating potential dispute on transfer or financing
exposure_statement.neutral: Quiet enjoyment scope, conditions, and survival against successors and lenders are undefined; both parties face uncertainty over tenant's right to undisturbed possession

negative_space_clues: Quiet enjoyment referenced in recitals or lease summary but no covenant in lease body
SNDA provision present but quiet enjoyment covenant absent
Landlord's representations section blank or marked Reserved
common_tenant_modifications: Covenant confirmed to bind lenders and mortgagees (coordinates with SNDA)
Absolute covenant for initial term (no conditioned-on-tenant-performance qualifier)
Explicit statement that landlord's right to re-enter does not breach quiet enjoyment covenant

expected_elements_305.element_label: Express covenant of quiet enjoyment is present in the lease
synonyms: Landlord covenants that Tenant shall peaceably and quietly hold and enjoy the Premises
Tenant shall have quiet possession of the Premises during the Term
expected_elements_305.review_notes: Pattern B: default-law and implicit coverage acceptable. In most US jurisdictions, the covenant of quiet enjoyment is implied by default in commercial leases. Absence of explicit covenant typically does NOT mean absence of coverage — default law covers. The schema should recognize 'silent on this element' as a covered-by-default outcome rather than missing. This is the canonical implicit-coverage test case from the architecture spec.

expected_elements_305.element_label: Scope of quiet enjoyment includes peaceful and undisturbed possession
synonyms: peaceably and quietly hold and enjoy
expected_elements_305.review_notes: Pattern B: scope is typically subsumed in the covenant of quiet enjoyment itself. Separate element exists for cases where the covenant is present but scope is narrowed by explicit language.

expected_elements_305.element_label: Tenant is protected from disturbance by landlord directly
synonyms: free from any disturbance by Landlord
Landlord shall not interfere with Tenant's possession
Landlord covenants not to disturb Tenant
expected_elements_305.review_notes: Pattern B: core element of quiet enjoyment. Implied by the covenant itself in most jurisdictions. Separate from third-party-claims element because the legal sources of disturbance differ.

expected_elements_305.element_label: Tenant is protected from claims by parties claiming through landlord (other tenants, lender, etc.)
synonyms: free from disturbance by anyone claiming through Landlord
free from claims by anyone claiming by, through, or under Landlord
free from any person claiming under Landlord
free from interference by other tenants of Landlord
expected_elements_305.review_notes: Pattern B: distinct from non-disturbance (LP-22) which addresses lender-foreclosure-successor scenarios. This element addresses ordinary third-party claims during the lease term (e.g., another tenant's encroachment authorized by landlord). The LP-22 → LP-26 cross-coverage block applies in the opposite direction: this element does NOT cover non-disturbance and non-disturbance does NOT cover this.

expected_elements_305.element_label: Quiet enjoyment is conditioned on tenant's performance of lease obligations
synonyms: so long as Tenant performs all of its obligations under this Lease
subject to Tenant's compliance with the terms hereof
provided Tenant is not in default
subject to the provisions of this Lease
expected_elements_305.review_notes: Pattern A: explicit text required. This is the one landlord-favorable element in an otherwise tenant-favorable LP. Conditioning language must be explicit to be enforceable; default law typically does not condition the implied covenant on tenant performance to the same extent. Presence is landlord-protective; absence is landlord-adverse (covenant remains in force even if tenant in breach).

expected_elements_305.element_label: Remedies for breach of quiet enjoyment are specified or cross-covered
synonyms: Tenant's remedies for breach of this covenant
remedies available at law or in equity
in addition to all remedies provided in this Lease
expected_elements_305.review_notes: Pattern B: legitimate cross-LP coverage to LP-27 (Landlord Default & Tenant Remedies). Breach of quiet enjoyment is a landlord default; LP-27 is where landlord-default remedies live. The cross-LP relationship is structurally legitimate. Note the directional asymmetry: LP-26 → LP-27 works (LP-27 houses landlord-default remedies generally); LP-26 → LP-22 does not work (quiet enjoyment is not non-disturbance). Step 305 evaluators must verify the LP-27 citation actually addresses landlord-default remedies and not merely the parallel structure.

expected_elements_305.element_label: Constructive eviction is acknowledged or addressed in the lease
synonyms: Tenant's right to vacate in case of substantial impairment
if Landlord's breach renders the Premises untenantable
expected_elements_305.review_notes: Pattern B: constructive eviction is a common-law doctrine available in most US jurisdictions even when not addressed in the lease. Explicit acknowledgment is procedurally cleaner but not legally necessary. Low absence severity because default-law coverage is reliable.

issue_areas.name: Landlord Default & Tenant Remedies
issue_areas.notes: The counterpart to LP-11 (tenant default). Often conspicuously weaker or absent in landlord-form leases ג€” landlords frequently attempt to limit tenant remedies to specific performance only, eliminating offset rights, self-help rights, and termination rights. The tenant's ability to offset rent against uncured landlord obligations is a major negotiating point.
expected_elements: definition of landlord default events (failure to perform material obligations after notice and cure)
notice and cure period before tenant may exercise remedies (typically 30 days written + additional reasonable time for complex repairs)
tenant self-help right to cure at landlord's expense after cure period expires
rent offset right against verified self-help costs
tenant's right to terminate on material uncured landlord default
lender third-party cure right (lender may cure landlord default within additional cure period)
limitation on landlord's personal liability (typically limited to interest in the property)

coverage_state_rules.missing: No landlord default provision found; tenant's remedies limited to state law defaults
coverage_state_rules.partial: Landlord default defined but self-help right, offset right, or termination right absent
coverage_state_rules.ambiguous: Landlord default clause present but remedies described as 'tenant's rights at law and equity' without enumeration
coverage_state_rules.covered_unfavorable: Tenant remedy limited to specific performance only (no termination, no offset, no self-help); OR notice and cure period so long as to render remedies impractical; OR landlord default provision explicitly excludes rent offset right

Tenant shall provide Landlord with notice of the alleged default
Tenant must deliver written notice describing the breach in reasonable detail
expected_elements_305.review_notes: Pattern A: explicit text required. Procedural protection for landlord. Absent notice requirement, tenant could declare default and exercise remedies without giving landlord opportunity to recognize and respond. Mirror of LP-11.notice_required_to_trigger_cure_period but polarity is reversed (this is landlord-favorable; LP-11 notice is tenant-favorable).

synonyms: Landlord shall have thirty (30) days after written notice to cure
cure period of thirty (30) days, or such longer period as may be reasonably necessary
Landlord shall commence cure within thirty (30) days and diligently prosecute to completion
expected_elements_305.review_notes: Pattern A: explicit text required. Cure period is typically longer than tenant's (often 30 days plus 'longer as reasonably necessary' extension). Mirror of LP-11.cure_period_non_monetary but applied to landlord. Polarity is reversed: presence of cure period is landlord-favorable here; in LP-11 presence was tenant-favorable. This is the cleanest single example of why severity-polarity split is required.

expected_elements_305.element_label: Tenant may perform landlord's obligation and offset against rent
synonyms: Tenant may perform such obligation and offset the cost against Rent
Tenant shall have the right to cure such default and deduct from Rent
amounts expended by Tenant shall be reimbursed by Landlord or, at Tenant's option, offset against Rent next due
expected_elements_305.review_notes: Pattern A: explicit text required. Powerful tenant remedy. Mirror of LP-11.self_help_landlord_cure but with the critical addition of rent offset. Landlord-side self-help bills tenant; tenant-side self-help reduces rent immediately. Without explicit grant, tenant typically has only damages remedy (no offset), which is much weaker.

expected_elements_305.element_label: Tenant has right to terminate the lease upon uncured landlord default
synonyms: Tenant shall have the right to terminate by written notice
Tenant may at its option terminate this Lease
Tenant may treat the Lease as terminated
expected_elements_305.review_notes: Pattern B (v0.2 correction): originally must_be_explicit=true with default_law=jurisdiction-dependent and implicit_coverage_acceptable=true — internally contradictory. Resolved by making must_be_explicit=false plus explicit_drafting_preferred=true. Default law in most jurisdictions allows tenant to terminate for material breach (constructive eviction or doctrine of material breach). Implicit coverage acceptable through these doctrines. Explicit grant is cleaner. Mirror of LP-11.landlord_right_to_terminate_lease but with stronger default-law backing because material-breach doctrine is broadly available. Note: cross_LP_coverage intentionally left null. Termination on landlord default is structurally distinct from termination on casualty (LP-13), condemnation (LP-14), or tenant default (LP-11) — those are separate scenarios with their own elements, not alternate sources of 'tenant right to terminate for landlord breach.'

expected_elements_305.element_label: Tenant has right to monetary damages for landlord default

Tenant may seek damages at law
Landlord shall be liable for all damages resulting from such default
damages including consequential, incidental, and direct
expected_elements_305.review_notes: Pattern B: default-law and implicit coverage acceptable. Default-law breach-of-contract damages available in all jurisdictions. Lease may limit recoverable damages (excluding consequential or punitive); such limits are landlord-favorable. Implicit coverage acceptable through breach-of-contract theory.

expected_elements_305.element_label: Tenant has right to specific performance or injunctive relief
synonyms: in addition to all other remedies, Tenant may seek equitable relief
expected_elements_305.review_notes: Pattern B: default-law and implicit coverage acceptable. Equitable remedies available by default in most jurisdictions for breach of unique-performance obligations (e.g., landlord's failure to deliver specific premises, build-out, or exclusive-use protections). Implicit coverage strong.

expected_elements_305.element_label: Tenant must notify lender and afford lender cure period before exercising remedies
synonyms: Tenant shall give simultaneous notice to any mortgagee
no remedy against Landlord may be exercised until any mortgagee has been notified
any mortgagee shall have an additional thirty (30) days to cure
expected_elements_305.review_notes: Pattern B (v0.2 correction, flagged for legal review): originally must_be_explicit=true with implicit_coverage_acceptable=true and cross_LP_coverage=[LP-22] — internally contradictory. Resolved by making must_be_explicit=false plus explicit_drafting_preferred=true, and flipping implicit_coverage_acceptable to false because the legitimate alternate path is cross-LP-via-SNDA (explicit-in-another-LP), not implicit-within-LP-27. Genuine cross-LP relationship to LP-22 SNDA: lender notice/cure rights are often defined in the SNDA rather than in LP-27 directly. Step 305 evaluators must cite the specific SNDA provision rather than gesturing at LP-22 generally. Polarity note: this element is landlord/lender-favorable; absence is landlord-adverse because lender can lose practical ability to step in and cure.

allocation of structural vs. use-specific compliance costs
ADA compliance allocation (structural = landlord; ADA modifications for tenant's specific operations = tenant)
future changes in law during the term (who bears the cost of code changes not triggered by tenant's use)
grandfathering for pre-existing non-compliant conditions at lease commencement

conflict_rules.description: Cross-provision logical conflicts. Each rule declares a pattern across two or more LPs that constitutes a conflict ג€” internal contradictions, missing prerequisites, or structural incoherence. Detected by lease_conflicts.py after coverage assessment completes.

rules.name: Force Majeure Abatement vs. Continuous Operation
rules.description: Force majeure abatement requires premises to be wholly untenantable, but the lease also requires continuous operation. Tenant must keep paying AND keep operating during partial impairment with no abatement available.

rules.name: SNDA Without Adequate Landlord Default Framework
rules.description: SNDA grants the lender a cure right for landlord defaults, but the lease's landlord default framework lacks meaningful tenant remedies ג€” tenant has no rent offset or termination right if the lender does not cure. The lender's cure right exists in form, but the tenant has limited recourse if remediation fails.

rules.name: No Exit Strategy: Restrictive Assignment + No Termination Right
rules.description: Assignment requires landlord consent (often with recapture right) and no early termination right exists. Tenant has no exit strategy if business fails ג€” must remain liable for full term with no transfer or termination mechanism.

jurisdiction_rules.description: State-specific rule applications. After coverage assessment completes, the governing law extracted from LP-17 is matched against this block. Matching rules may escalate or reclassify coverage states for LPs flagged with governing_law_sensitive caution. Applied by lease_jurisdiction.py before lease_conflicts.py runs.
jurisdiction_rules.fallback_behavior: If governing law is not extracted or not in this rules dict, no jurisdiction-aware escalations are applied. Coverage assessment uses base classifications.

rules.rationale: NY courts imply reasonableness in commercial lease consent provisions absent explicit contrary language. Real Property Law ֲ§226-c and case law suggest sole discretion may be unenforceable.
NY strongly disfavors self-help eviction. RPAPL ֲ§853 provides treble damages for forcible entry. Yellowstone injunction available to tenants facing aggressive default actions.
